display.title: Episode 371: The Blessing of a Tzaddik, Chapter 1 (Rosh Chodesh Nissan)
display.summary_short: Before Rosh Chodesh Nissan: nature is Hashem's greatest miracle, why a tzaddik's brachah is like rain, and Reb Boruch's mysterious night at a snowbound inn.
display.summary_long: Broadcast just before Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5749. Uncle Yossi explains that the name Nissan comes from 'neis', miracle: the Ten Plagues and the splitting of the sea, where the Midrash says the seabed was covered with grass. Yet we do not need miracles to know Hashem; the sunrise, the stars and fruit trees are His acts too, and nature itself is the greatest miracle. Strong emunah will bring the greatest miracle of all, Moshiach, in Nissan. After the Hakochainik march, story time opens with a teaching: Hashem gave Avraham Avinu the power to bless, as Rashi explains, and tzaddikim in every generation share it. A tzaddik's brachah is like rain, which only helps soil that has been cleared and plowed; mitzvos draw the brachah and aveiros block it. The story begins: Reb Boruch reaches an inn in a blinding snowstorm after midnight and will not wake an old man sleeping by the fire. A five-year-old leads the Shema, and then a young man comes down the stairs and sharply orders the old man to show the guest his room. Reb Boruch is puzzled: who is that young man? The answer comes next week. A boy's letter asks if his whole family can visit Studio 604.
display.lesson: Nature itself is Hashem's miracle; and to receive a tzaddik's blessing we must prepare ourselves with mitzvos, like soil ready for rain.
